actual_scope: Characteristic polynomial, over Q(i), of the eigenvalue-i eigenspace of s=(0 4 3 7)(5 6) on the moved c=1 sign character eps[1]*eps[2]. The polynomial lies in Z[x]. The eigenvalue -i space of the same character is isospectral.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for a formal caller or certificate binding. PR #7036 leaves the characteristic polynomial, over Q(i), of one eigenvalue-i eigenspace of s on eps[1]*eps[2] uncomputed. The integer basis in that PR solves only the eigenvalues ±1. This package answers that polynomial. It does not add a Lean binding.
bottleneck_link: Scoped side result on the historical centre Gram. The selected conditional kappa remains 781451/250000000. The one-slot minimal polynomial remains degree 881 in research/exact-one-slot-gram/; this polynomial locates the eigenvalue-i subspace of one moved 192-character inside that certificate and does not replace it.
stop_rule: Stop once one explicit 48-dimensional Q(i) basis and the characteristic polynomial of A_1 on it are recomputed from the pinned query, with the matrix pinned and the factorization over Q(i) checked. Do not compute the geometric multiplicity, and do not compute the eigenvalue-i polynomial on eps[5]*eps[6].
evidence: verify.py rebuilds the Q(i) basis and the 48-by-48 matrix of B=4 A_1 over Z[i]. open_questions.question: What is the geometric multiplicity of eigenvalue 0 for A_1 on this pinned eigenvalue-i matrix?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The characteristic polynomial gives algebraic multiplicity 10 and is not square-free, so it is not the minimal polynomial. The nullity of the pinned matrix over Q(i) is the geometric multiplicity. This is not the eigenvalue-+1 matrix of PR #7036.
open_questions.first_step: Compute the exact rank over Q(i) of the pinned 48-by-48 matrix of B.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package interpolates the characteristic polynomial and does not run the exact elimination for the kernel.

open_questions.question: What is the characteristic polynomial, over Q(i), of one eigenvalue-i eigenspace of s on the character eps[5]*eps[6]?
open_questions.why_it_matters: s preserves a second 192-dimensional character. The polynomial computed here is for eps[1]*eps[2] only. PR #7036 already shows that the two characters are not isospectral on the eigenvalue-+1 spaces.
open_questions.first_step: Repeat the least-index Q(i) orbit basis for eps[5]*eps[6] and interpolate det(xI-B) on that basis.
open_questions.blocked_by: The basis pinned here solves only eps[1]*eps[2].
